20	// recur often enough to be worth writing by hand, each with the exact edit that
21	// satisfies it. A rule absent from the catalog is not a gap to be filled. It is
22	// the case the MCP server already covers, by handing a calling agent the span,
23	// the wording and the file (phase A) and re-measuring afterwards.
24	//
25	// That boundary is the point, and it is why Fix declines instead of
26	// approximating: an absence sends the user to something that works, while a
27	// doubtful edit sends them to a diff they have to second-guess.
28	
29	// Rule is one misconfiguration this application knows how to fix on its own.
30	type Rule struct {
31		// AVDID is the rule's identity as Trivy reports it in Finding.ID. It is
32		// matched loosely — see ruleKey — because Trivy spells the same rule
33		// "AVD-DS-0002" in one field and "DS002" in another.
34		AVDID string
35		// Title is what the UI calls the fix. It says what the edit does, not what
36		// the rule forbids: the user is agreeing to a change, not reading an advisory.
37		Title string
38		// Fix returns the edits that satisfy the rule on content, or nil and a
39		// reason when this instance is not one the catalog handles.
40		//
41		// It never guesses. An instance it cannot read exactly is one it declines,
42		// and the reason is shown to the user as-is (Rule 129: English).
43		Fix func(content []byte, f scan.Finding) ([]patch.Edit, string)
44		// Warning is a sentence the confirmation shows with the diff when the
45		// fix reverses a choice the author may have made on purpose (DEVDESK-687).
46		// Empty for a fix that has nothing to warn about.
47		Warning string

330	// RuleKey reduces the spellings of one rule id to a single key.
331	//
332	// Trivy writes "AVD-DS-0002" in AVDID and "DS002" in ID, and which of the two
333	// reaches a Finding has changed before. Matching on either spelling costs one
334	// function; matching on one of them costs a catalog that silently stops firing
335	// the day the other is used.
336	func RuleKey(id string) string {
337		id = strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(id))
338		id = strings.TrimPrefix(id, "AVD-")
339		id = strings.ReplaceAll(id, "-", "")
340	
341		letters := strings.IndexFunc(id, func(r rune) bool { return r >= '0' && r <= '9' })
342		if letters <= 0 {
343			return id
344		}
345		prefix, digits := id[:letters], strings.TrimLeft(id[letters:], "0")
346		if digits == "" {
347			digits = "0"
348		}
349		return prefix + digits

132	// ecosystem with no known command, the plain instruction the finding always

134	func trivyFixCommand(ecosystem string, vuln TrivyVulnerability) string {
135		target := PickFixed(vuln.InstalledVersion, vuln.FixedVersion)
136		if target == "" {
137			if vuln.FixedVersion == "" {
138				return ""
139			}
140			target = vuln.FixedVersion
141		}
142		if cmd, ok := FixCommand(ecosystem, vuln.PkgName, target); ok {
143			return cmd

148	// mergeRefs is the reference list of a finding: primary first, then the other
149	// references in their order, without duplicates.
150	func mergeRefs(primary string, refs []string) []string {
151		out := make([]string, 0, len(refs)+1)
152		if primary != "" {
153			out = append(out, primary)
154		}
155		for _, r := range refs {
156			if r != "" && !slices.Contains(out, r) {
157				out = append(out, r)
158			}
159		}
160		return out

163	// parseTrivyOutput parses Trivy JSON output into findings
164	func parseTrivyOutput(data []byte) ([]Finding, error) {
165		var report TrivyReport
166		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &report); err != nil {
167			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse trivy output: %w", err)
168		}
169	
170		var findings []Finding
171	
172		for _, result := range report.Results {
173			// Process vulnerabilities
174			for _, vuln := range result.Vulnerabilities {
175				refs := mergeRefs(vuln.PrimaryURL, vuln.References)
176	
177				// Build a fix command suggestion when a fixed version is known
178				fixCmd := trivyFixCommand(result.Type, vuln)
179	
180				findings = append(findings, Finding{
181					ID:          vuln.VulnerabilityID,
182					Title:       vuln.Title,
183					Description: vuln.Description,
184					Severity:    parseSeverity(vuln.Severity),
185					Source:      "trivy",
186					File:        result.Target,
187					PkgName:     vuln.PkgName,
188					Version:     vuln.InstalledVersion,
189					FixedIn:     vuln.FixedVersion,
190					Class:       result.Class,
191					Ecosystem:   result.Type,
192					References:  refs,
193					FixCommand:  fixCmd,
194				})
195			}
196	
197			// Process secrets found by Trivy.
198			//
199			// The report has carried these since TrivySecret was declared; nothing
200			// read them, so a secret Trivy found was parsed and dropped. Only the
201			// secret stage asks for them (--scanners secret), so there is no risk of
202			// the vulnerability stage returning the same finding twice.
203			for _, secret := range result.Secrets {
204				findings = append(findings, Finding{
205					ID:          secret.RuleID,
206					Title:       secret.Title,
207					Description: secret.Category,
208					Severity:    parseSeverity(secret.Severity),
209					Source:      SourceTrivySecret,
210					File:        result.Target,
211					Line:        secret.StartLine,
212					Match:       maskSecret(secret.Match),
213				})
214			}
215	
216			// Process licenses found by Trivy
217			for _, license := range result.Licenses {
218				findings = append(findings, Finding{
219					ID:          license.Name,
220					Title:       fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", license.PkgName, license.Name),
221					Description: fmt.Sprintf("License category: %s", license.Category),
222					Severity:    parseSeverity(license.Severity),
223					Source:      "trivy-license",
224					File:        license.FilePath,
225					PkgName:     license.PkgName,
226				})
227			}
228	
229			// Process misconfigurations found by Trivy
230			for _, misconf := range result.Misconfigurations {
231				findings = append(findings, Finding{
232					ID:          firstNonEmpty(misconf.AVDID, misconf.ID),
233					Title:       misconf.Title,
234					Description: misconf.Desc,
235					Severity:    parseSeverity(misconf.Severity),
236					Source:      "trivy-misconfig",
237					File:        result.Target,
238					Line:        misconf.CauseMetadata.StartLine,
239					EndLine:     misconf.CauseMetadata.EndLine,
240					Message:     misconf.Message,
241					Status:      misconf.Status,
242					// The result's type, not the misconfiguration's own: that one
243					// is a label ("Kubernetes Security Check"), this one the
244					// dialect ("kubernetes").
245					IaCType:    strings.ToLower(result.Type),
246					Resolution: misconf.Resolution,
247					References: mergeRefs(misconf.PrimaryURL, misconf.References),
248				})
249			}
250		}
251	
252		return findings, nil
253	}

255	// parseSeverity converts string severity to SeverityLevel
256	func parseSeverity(s string) SeverityLevel {
257		switch strings.ToUpper(s) {
258		case "CRITICAL":

262		case "MEDIUM":
263			return SeverityMedium
264		case "LOW":

20	// findingColumns describes the findings table.
21	//
22	// The table opens on the order the scanner reported — `SortColumn: -1`, which
23	// datatable keeps as a stop on the cycle, so `.` always leads back to it. Every
24	// column sorts, because `.` was handed back to the sort when the severity floor
25	// became four tokens (§3.26) and then no column was ever given a `Less`:
26	// CycleSort returned on its first line and the header advertised a key that did
27	// nothing at all.
28	//
29	// Three columns search, and that is not optional either. Declaring tokens makes
30	// `Searchable()` true, so `/` already opened a query — against no searchable
31	// column, which matches nothing and empties the table. The bar's own left half
32	// says `/ search...` whether or not anything answers it.
33	//
34	// Severity searches nothing on purpose: c/h/m/l are the severity filter, and a
35	// second way to ask one question is what this codebase spends its time
36	// removing. The Title is not pre-truncated either — bubbles cuts every cell to
37	// its column width with the same ellipsis, and doing it by hand at width-3
38	// first only cost three characters of title.
39	func findingColumns() []datatable.Column[scan.Finding] {
40		return []datatable.Column[scan.Finding]{
41			{
42				Title: "Severity", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 10,

45				// same colour whether or not the cursor is on it.
46				Style: func(f scan.Finding) lipgloss.Style { return theme.SeverityTextStyle(string(f.Severity)) },
47				Less:  func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return severityRank(a.Severity) < severityRank(b.Severity) },
48			},

72	// severityRank orders the levels by how bad they are, which is the only order

83	func severityRank(s scan.SeverityLevel) int {

3	import (

7	)
8	
9	// missingRule is what a Pod Security rule without a fix asks of the manifest:
10	// the rule as it is written for the user, the field with the value the profile
11	// expects, and what is worth knowing besides. Every entry was read in the source
12	// of the Trivy check (the checks bundle the recorded output was made with,
13	// testdata/pss/), none from memory of the standard.
14	//
15	// The text is read in a footer that keeps one line and cuts it with an ellipsis,
16	// 80 columns being the narrow case: need is what comes first and must fit after
17	// the prefix; detail comes last and may be the part that is cut.
18	type missingRule struct {
19		id     string
20		need   string
21		detail string
22	}
23	
24	// missingRules is keyed by RuleKey. It holds the rules of the Pod Security table
25	// that have no fix of their own; a rule with a fix (KSV-0017, KSV-0001,
26	// KSV-0008 to KSV-0010) is absent on purpose, so its confirmation diff is what
27	// the user sees. KSV-0030 and KSV-0104 have a fix since DEVDESK-688 and stay
28	// here: the text is shown only for a KSV-0104 Unconfined, which the fix never
29	// touches and greys in advance. Every other refusal of the seccomp fix shows its
30	// own ReasonSeccomp* reason at the press of the key, not this text. KSV-0104 is
31	// handled apart because its text depends on SeccompOrigin.
32	var missingRules = map[string]missingRule{
33		RuleKey("KSV-0103"): {"KSV-0103", "set windowsOptions.hostProcess to false, or remove it", ""},
34		RuleKey("KSV-0022"): {"KSV-0022", "remove capabilities.add", "Trivy's check is stricter than Pod Security, which allows a list of capabilities"},
35		RuleKey("KSV-0023"): {"KSV-0023", "remove the hostPath entries of volumes", ""},
36		RuleKey("KSV-0024"): {"KSV-0024", "remove hostPort from the container ports", ""},
37		RuleKey("KSV-0002"): {"KSV-0002", "set the AppArmor annotation to runtime/default", "the annotation is container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/<container>"},
38		RuleKey("KSV-0025"): {"KSV-0025", "set seLinuxOptions.type to container_t, no role or user", "container_init_t and container_kvm_t are allowed too; any seLinuxOptions.role or user fails"},
39		RuleKey("KSV-0026"): {"KSV-0026", "keep sysctls names in the allowed list", "such as kernel.shm_rmid_forced, in securityContext.sysctls"},
40		RuleKey("KSV-0027"): {"KSV-0027", "remove procMount", "even Default fails"},
41		RuleKey("KSV-0028"): {"KSV-0028", "limit volumes to allowed types (emptyDir, not nfs)", ""},
42		RuleKey("KSV-0012"): {"KSV-0012", "set runAsNonRoot to true", "on the pod, or on every container"},
43		RuleKey("KSV-0105"): {"KSV-0105", "set runAsUser to a value greater than 0", ""},
44		RuleKey("KSV-0106"): {"KSV-0106", "capabilities.drop needs ALL, add only NET_BIND_SERVICE", ""},
45		RuleKey("KSV-0121"): {"KSV-0121", "do not mount a hostPath on /, /boot, /dev, /etc, /lib, /proc, /sys, /usr or /var/lib/docker", ""},
46		RuleKey("KSV-0030"): {"KSV-0030", "set seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault", "on the pod or on the container"},
47	}
48	
49	// seccompNeed is the text of KSV-0104 for each origin of the finding.
50	func seccompNeed(origin string) (need, detail string) {
51		switch origin {
52		case "unconfined":
53			return "set seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault, not Unconfined", ""
54		case "absent":
55			return "set seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault", "seccompProfile is not set"
56		default:
57			return "set seccompProfile", ""
58		}
59	}
60	
61	// MissingFor is the text of the refusal for a Pod Security finding DevDesk has
62	// no safe fix for (DEVDESK-689, S-04): the field to set and the value the
63	// finding's profile expects. The boolean is false when there is nothing to say,
64	// that is when f is not a Pod Security finding, or when its rule has a fix of
65	// its own.
66	//
67	// A rule whose profile was read in Trivy (not in the table) gets a text that
68	// says so and names no field: DevDesk knows nothing else about it.
69	func MissingFor(f scan.Finding) (string, bool) {
70		pss, ok := PodSecurity(f)
71		if !ok {
72			return "", false
73		}
74		if pss.FromTrivy {
75			return fmt.Sprintf("%s: the %s Pod Security profile comes from Trivy. DevDesk has no fix and no text for this rule; see the check's description in Trivy", f.ID, pss.Profile), true
76		}
77		key := RuleKey(f.ID)
78		if key == ruleSeccomp {
79			need, detail := seccompNeed(f.SeccompOrigin)
80			return missingText(pss.Profile, "KSV-0104", need, detail), true
81		}
82		r, ok := missingRules[key]
83		if !ok {
84			return "", false
85		}
86		return missingText(pss.Profile, r.id, r.need, r.detail), true
87	}
88	
89	// missingText puts the rule, its profile and what it asks in one sentence, the
90	// need right after a short prefix, then the fact that the finding has no fix,
91	// then the detail. It does not offer a fix: the finding has none.
92	func missingText(p Profile, id, need, detail string) string {
93		text := fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s): %s (no built-in fix)", id, p, need)
94		if detail != "" {
95			text += " — " + detail
96		}
97		return text
98	}

9	// missingRule is what a Pod Security rule without a fix asks of the manifest:
10	// the rule as it is written for the user, the field with the value the profile
11	// expects, and what is worth knowing besides. Every entry was read in the source
12	// of the Trivy check (the checks bundle the recorded output was made with,
13	// testdata/pss/), none from memory of the standard.
14	//
15	// The text is read in a footer that keeps one line and cuts it with an ellipsis,
16	// 80 columns being the narrow case: need is what comes first and must fit after
17	// the prefix; detail comes last and may be the part that is cut.
18	type missingRule struct {
19		id     string
20		need   string
21		detail string
22	}
23	
24	// missingRules is keyed by RuleKey. It holds the rules of the Pod Security table
25	// that have no fix of their own; a rule with a fix (KSV-0017, KSV-0001,
26	// KSV-0008 to KSV-0010) is absent on purpose, so its confirmation diff is what
27	// the user sees. KSV-0030 and KSV-0104 have a fix since DEVDESK-688 and stay
28	// here: the text is shown only for a KSV-0104 Unconfined, which the fix never
29	// touches and greys in advance. Every other refusal of the seccomp fix shows its
30	// own ReasonSeccomp* reason at the press of the key, not this text. KSV-0104 is
31	// handled apart because its text depends on SeccompOrigin.
32	var missingRules = map[string]missingRule{
33		RuleKey("KSV-0103"): {"KSV-0103", "set windowsOptions.hostProcess to false, or remove it", ""},
34		RuleKey("KSV-0022"): {"KSV-0022", "remove capabilities.add", "Trivy's check is stricter than Pod Security, which allows a list of capabilities"},
35		RuleKey("KSV-0023"): {"KSV-0023", "remove the hostPath entries of volumes", ""},
36		RuleKey("KSV-0024"): {"KSV-0024", "remove hostPort from the container ports", ""},
37		RuleKey("KSV-0002"): {"KSV-0002", "set the AppArmor annotation to runtime/default", "the annotation is container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/<container>"},
38		RuleKey("KSV-0025"): {"KSV-0025", "set seLinuxOptions.type to container_t, no role or user", "container_init_t and container_kvm_t are allowed too; any seLinuxOptions.role or user fails"},
39		RuleKey("KSV-0026"): {"KSV-0026", "keep sysctls names in the allowed list", "such as kernel.shm_rmid_forced, in securityContext.sysctls"},
40		RuleKey("KSV-0027"): {"KSV-0027", "remove procMount", "even Default fails"},
41		RuleKey("KSV-0028"): {"KSV-0028", "limit volumes to allowed types (emptyDir, not nfs)", ""},
42		RuleKey("KSV-0012"): {"KSV-0012", "set runAsNonRoot to true", "on the pod, or on every container"},
43		RuleKey("KSV-0105"): {"KSV-0105", "set runAsUser to a value greater than 0", ""},
44		RuleKey("KSV-0106"): {"KSV-0106", "capabilities.drop needs ALL, add only NET_BIND_SERVICE", ""},
45		RuleKey("KSV-0121"): {"KSV-0121", "do not mount a hostPath on /, /boot, /dev, /etc, /lib, /proc, /sys, /usr or /var/lib/docker", ""},
46		RuleKey("KSV-0030"): {"KSV-0030", "set seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault", "on the pod or on the container"},
47	}

49	// seccompNeed is the text of KSV-0104 for each origin of the finding.
50	func seccompNeed(origin string) (need, detail string) {
51		switch origin {
52		case "unconfined":
53			return "set seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault, not Unconfined", ""
54		case "absent":
55			return "set seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault", "seccompProfile is not set"
56		default:
57			return "set seccompProfile", ""
58		}
59	}

61	// MissingFor is the text of the refusal for a Pod Security finding DevDesk has
62	// no safe fix for (DEVDESK-689, S-04): the field to set and the value the
63	// finding's profile expects. The boolean is false when there is nothing to say,
64	// that is when f is not a Pod Security finding, or when its rule has a fix of
65	// its own.
66	//
67	// A rule whose profile was read in Trivy (not in the table) gets a text that
68	// says so and names no field: DevDesk knows nothing else about it.
69	func MissingFor(f scan.Finding) (string, bool) {
70		pss, ok := PodSecurity(f)
71		if !ok {
72			return "", false
73		}
74		if pss.FromTrivy {
75			return fmt.Sprintf("%s: the %s Pod Security profile comes from Trivy. DevDesk has no fix and no text for this rule; see the check's description in Trivy", f.ID, pss.Profile), true
76		}
77		key := RuleKey(f.ID)
78		if key == ruleSeccomp {
79			need, detail := seccompNeed(f.SeccompOrigin)
80			return missingText(pss.Profile, "KSV-0104", need, detail), true
81		}
82		r, ok := missingRules[key]
83		if !ok {
84			return "", false
85		}
86		return missingText(pss.Profile, r.id, r.need, r.detail), true
87	}
88	
89	// missingText puts the rule, its profile and what it asks in one sentence, the
90	// need right after a short prefix, then the fact that the finding has no fix,
91	// then the detail. It does not offer a fix: the finding has none.
92	func missingText(p Profile, id, need, detail string) string {
93		text := fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s): %s (no built-in fix)", id, p, need)
94		if detail != "" {
95			text += " — " + detail
96		}
97		return text
98	}

1	// Package keymap declares the application's keyboard vocabulary.
2	//
3	// It does not read any key and does not depend on bubbletea: it is a list of
4	// strings, and its only role is to be the reference the tests check the code
5	// against (keymap_test.go). Without this reference, key consistency is a
6	// convention that nothing verifies — which is exactly the state §3.26 found:
7	// 184 bindings, 16 collisions.
8	//
9	// # Three disjoint namespaces
10	//
11	//   - An UPPERCASE letter is an action, and its meaning is global to the
12	//     application. `D` deletes, in every view, whatever "delete" means
13	//     wherever you are.
14	//   - A lowercase letter is a filter or a display toggle. It changes
15	//     nothing, so its meaning can be local and two views can use the same
16	//     letter without contradicting each other.
17	//   - Everything else (arrows, esc, enter, tab, space, `/`, `.`, `?`, `:`) is
18	//     structural and never changes.
19	//
20	// # Why Shift carries the actions
21	//
22	// This isn't a matter of taste, it's the real budget of a terminal:
23	//
24	//	Ctrl+letter  : only encodes ASCII 0x40-0x5F, and the tty confiscates
25	//	               four of them (ctrl+i = TAB, ctrl+m = Enter, ctrl+j = LF,
26	//	               ctrl+h = Backspace). ctrl+a and ctrl+b are screen's and
27	//	               tmux's prefixes, ctrl+c/ctrl+d are SIGINT and EOF,
28	//	               ctrl+s/ctrl+q are flow control.           → ~14 left
29	//	Alt+key      : Option is not Meta on macOS unless the user enables it;
30	//	               the application receives nothing.                → 0
31	//	Ctrl+Shift   : the control code erases case — ctrl+a and ctrl+shift+a
32	//	               both emit 0x01. Telling them apart requires the Kitty
33	//	               keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys, which bubbletea
34	//	               v1.3.10 does not enable (that's WithKeyboardEnhancements()
35	//	               in v2). And even then the emulator claims them first:
36	//	               ctrl+shift+c/v/t/w/n are copy, paste, tab, close, window.
37	//	                                                                  → 0
38	//	Shift+letter : no constraint. Works on every emulator, every platform,
39	//	               through SSH and tmux.                             → 26
40	//
41	// Shift+letter IS a two-key combination: two fingers, no accidental firing.
42	// It carries the vocabulary not by default, but because the two other
43	// families are crippled or unusable.
44	package keymap
45	
46	import (
47		"maps"
48		"sort"
49		"strings"
50	)
51	
52	// The 24 actions. About forty actions used to exist for 26 letters: the
53	// rule only holds after merging synonyms (Kill = stop and kill,
54	// Delete = delete and remove, Terminal = terminal and shell) and because
55	// display toggles are excluded from the count.
56	const (
57		New      = "N" // Create a resource from this context
58		Edit     = "E" // Edit the selected resource
59		Delete   = "D" // Delete the selected resource
60		Rename   = "M" // Rename (mv)
61		Scan     = "S" // Scan the selected target
62		ScanAll  = "A" // Scan everything (modal: "purge the cache first" checkbox)
63		Fetch    = "F" // Catch up with the source: fetch + fast-forward, or follow a stream
64		Clone    = "C" // Enter clone selection
65		Terminal = "T" // Open a terminal or shell
66		IDE      = "O" // Open in the configured IDE
67		Web      = "W" // Open a URL in the browser
68		Logs     = "L" // Open the logs
69		Pager    = "V" // Open in the system pager
70		Kill     = "K" // Stop, kill (modal: Stop / Restart, or SIGKILL)
71		Prune    = "P" // Remove unused resources
72		Browser  = "B" // Open the multi-registry browser
73		Get      = "G" // Pull (get) the image or tag
74		Auth     = "U" // Login / logout of the registry — toggles based on the row's state
75		Exclude  = "X" // Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore
76		Requests = "R" // Open merge requests · PRs
77		Issues   = "I" // Open issues
78		Diagnose = "H" // Open network diagnostics on this target
79		// Jump took J from the free letters: it opens the selected row's related
80		// resource in the view that owns it — the image a container runs, today.
81		Jump = "J" // Jump to the related resource in its own view
82		// Copy is `Y` — yank. The letter was free even though a modal uses it
83		// for "Yes": a modal claims every key before the view sees it, so the
84		// two are never reachable at the same time.
85		Copy = "Y" // Copy the obvious thing to the clipboard — a path, a document's content, the MCP connect command
86	)
87	
88	// CommandMode opens the command palette, from anywhere — including from a
89	// focused text field.
90	//
91	// ctrl+p, and not ctrl+: : ":" is 0x3A, outside the 0x40-0x5F range Ctrl
92	// encodes, so "ctrl+:" never reaches the application. The fallback was
93	// alt+:, which has the opposite flaw: on Terminal.app and iTerm2,
94	// Option+Shift+; emits a literal character and the key doesn't arrive
95	// either. ctrl+p is free throughout the application, is not a tty control
96	// character, is not the prefix of any multiplexer, and its meaning is
97	// already learned — command palette.
98	const CommandMode = "ctrl+p"
99	
100	// Space is the space key as KeyPressMsg.String() reports it in bubbletea v2
101	// ("space"). Code matches it through this name, never through a literal.
102	const Space = "space"
103	
104	// actions maps each action key to its meaning. This is the table the tests
105	// check the code against; the table in §3.26 is its readable form.
106	var actions = map[string]string{
107		New:      "Create a resource from this context",
108		Edit:     "Edit the selected resource",
109		Delete:   "Delete the selected resource",
110		Rename:   "Rename",
111		Scan:     "Scan the selected target",
112		ScanAll:  "Scan everything",
113		Fetch:    "Catch up with the source",
114		Clone:    "Enter clone selection",
115		Terminal: "Open a terminal or shell",
116		IDE:      "Open in the configured IDE",
117		Web:      "Open a URL in the browser",
118		Logs:     "Open the logs",
119		Pager:    "Open in the system pager",
120		Kill:     "Stop or kill",
121		Prune:    "Remove unused resources",
122		Browser:  "Open the multi-registry browser",
123		Get:      "Pull the image or tag",
124		Auth:     "Log in or out of the registry",
125		Exclude:  "Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore",
126		Requests: "Open merge requests · PRs",
127		Issues:   "Open issues",
128		Diagnose: "Open network diagnostics on this target",
129		Jump:     "Jump to the related resource in its own view",
130		Copy:     "Copy the obvious thing to the clipboard",
131	}

133	// Actions returns a copy of the key → meaning table.
134	func Actions() map[string]string {
135		out := make(map[string]string, len(actions))
136		maps.Copy(out, actions)
137		return out
138	}
139	
140	// IsAction reports whether a key belongs to the action vocabulary.
141	func IsAction(key string) bool {
142		_, ok := actions[key]
143		return ok
144	}
145	
146	// modalKeys are the shortcuts of a confirmation modal.
147	//
148	// This is a fourth namespace, and it is disjoint from the other three by
149	// mode rather than by case: a modal claims every key before the view sees
150	// it (priority 1 in every handleKeyMsg), so `N` cannot mean "create" there
151	// — the view underneath receives nothing. Same argument as for InEditMode.
152	//
153	// They are declared here because the §3.26 survey had not seen them, and
154	// an uppercase letter bound without a declaration is indistinguishable
155	// from drift.
156	var modalKeys = map[string]string{
157		"y": "Yes", "Y": "Yes",
158		"n": "No", "N": "No",
159	}
160	
161	// ModalKeys returns the modal shortcuts.
162	func ModalKeys() map[string]string {
163		out := make(map[string]string, len(modalKeys))
164		maps.Copy(out, modalKeys)
165		return out
166	}
167	
168	// IsModalKey reports whether a key is a modal shortcut.
169	func IsModalKey(key string) bool {
170		_, ok := modalKeys[key]
171		return ok
172	}
173	
174	// free lists the uppercase letters no action occupies. They are declared
175	// rather than left to be inferred: the next addition must know where to
176	// pick from without redoing the survey, and an action that settles
177	// somewhere other than here is a duplicate that goes unnoticed.
178	// H came back here with §3.47 (it used to trace the route, removed because
179	// it answered for the Docker VM rather than for the machine, D57) and left
180	// again with Diagnose (§3.66): a good semantic fit for "look closer at this
181	// target's network path." A letter an action has just freed up is
182	// re-declared free, otherwise it stays reserved for a use that no longer
183	// exists. J left with Jump (a container's image, opened in the OCI view).
184	var free = []string{"Q", "Z"}
185	
186	// Free returns the still-available uppercase letters, sorted.
187	func Free() []string {
188		out := append([]string(nil), free...)
189		sort.Strings(out)
190		return out
191	}
192	
193	// Surface is a screen, its files, and the lowercase letters it uses.
194	//
195	// Path is what ties a file to its surface, and it is there so the
196	// declaration is checkable: without it, "these letters are local to this
197	// view" is verified by merging every list, and `l` declared for netdiag
198	// would excuse `l` in the registries. Matching is done on the longest
199	// prefix, so netdiag/ports can narrow down netdiag.
200	type Surface struct {
201		Name string
202		Path string
203		Keys []string
204	}
205	
206	// localToggles inventories the lowercase letters used as display or filter
207	// toggles. They change nothing, so their meaning is local and the same
208	// letter can serve twice without contradiction — `l` is the protocol in
209	// netdiag and the LOW severity in security.
210	//
211	// A file that matches no surface is entitled to no lowercase letter at
212	// all: that is the default, and it is what makes the list worth keeping
213	// up to date.
214	var localToggles = []Surface{
215		{"containers", "ui/containers/", []string{"r", "p", "s", "t", "z"}},
216		{"viewer", "ui/viewer/", []string{"f", "c", "w", "v", "t", "n", "g", "s"}},
217		{"netdiag/ports", "ui/netdiag/ports_model.go", []string{"t", "u", "l", "e", "n", "z"}},
218		{"netdiag/checks", "ui/netdiag/", []string{"p"}},
219		{"oci/browser", "ui/oci_resources/browser_", []string{"r"}},
220		{"security/findings", "ui/security/", []string{"c", "h", "m", "l", "p"}},
221		// g opens the fuzzy-find prompt across the whole workspaces tree. Same
222		// justification as the viewer's g: the jump takes an argument (the typed
223		// query), which is not a role home/end/G could ever cover.
224		{"workspaces", "ui/workspaces/", []string{"g"}},
225		// The same prompt over the forge index: every namespace and repository
226		// the session can see, at any depth.
227		{"forge/explorer", "ui/forge/explorer/", []string{"g"}},
228	}
229	
230	// LocalToggles returns the declared surfaces.
231	func LocalToggles() []Surface {
232		return append([]Surface(nil), localToggles...)
233	}
234	
235	// SurfaceFor ties a file path to its surface, by longest prefix. The
236	// second return says whether a surface was found.
237	func SurfaceFor(path string) (Surface, bool) {
238		var best Surface
239		found := false
240		for _, s := range localToggles {
241			if !strings.Contains(path, s.Path) {
242				continue
243			}
244			if !found || len(s.Path) > len(best.Path) {
245				best, found = s, true
246			}
247		}
248		return best, found
249	}
250	
251	// Exception is a key that deviates from the vocabulary, with its reason.
252	type Exception struct {
253		Key     string
254		Surface string
255		Why     string
256	}
257

1	// Package keymap declares the application's keyboard vocabulary.
2	//
3	// It does not read any key and does not depend on bubbletea: it is a list of
4	// strings, and its only role is to be the reference the tests check the code
5	// against (keymap_test.go). Without this reference, key consistency is a
6	// convention that nothing verifies — which is exactly the state §3.26 found:
7	// 184 bindings, 16 collisions.
8	//
9	// # Three disjoint namespaces
10	//
11	//   - An UPPERCASE letter is an action, and its meaning is global to the
12	//     application. `D` deletes, in every view, whatever "delete" means
13	//     wherever you are.
14	//   - A lowercase letter is a filter or a display toggle. It changes
15	//     nothing, so its meaning can be local and two views can use the same
16	//     letter without contradicting each other.
17	//   - Everything else (arrows, esc, enter, tab, space, `/`, `.`, `?`, `:`) is
18	//     structural and never changes.
19	//
20	// # Why Shift carries the actions
21	//
22	// This isn't a matter of taste, it's the real budget of a terminal:
23	//
24	//	Ctrl+letter  : only encodes ASCII 0x40-0x5F, and the tty confiscates
25	//	               four of them (ctrl+i = TAB, ctrl+m = Enter, ctrl+j = LF,
26	//	               ctrl+h = Backspace). ctrl+a and ctrl+b are screen's and
27	//	               tmux's prefixes, ctrl+c/ctrl+d are SIGINT and EOF,
28	//	               ctrl+s/ctrl+q are flow control.           → ~14 left
29	//	Alt+key      : Option is not Meta on macOS unless the user enables it;
30	//	               the application receives nothing.                → 0
31	//	Ctrl+Shift   : the control code erases case — ctrl+a and ctrl+shift+a
32	//	               both emit 0x01. Telling them apart requires the Kitty
33	//	               keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys, which bubbletea
34	//	               v1.3.10 does not enable (that's WithKeyboardEnhancements()
35	//	               in v2). And even then the emulator claims them first:
36	//	               ctrl+shift+c/v/t/w/n are copy, paste, tab, close, window.
37	//	                                                                  → 0
38	//	Shift+letter : no constraint. Works on every emulator, every platform,
39	//	               through SSH and tmux.                             → 26
40	//
41	// Shift+letter IS a two-key combination: two fingers, no accidental firing.
42	// It carries the vocabulary not by default, but because the two other
43	// families are crippled or unusable.

47		"maps"
48		"sort"
49		"strings"
50	)

52	// The 24 actions. About forty actions used to exist for 26 letters: the
53	// rule only holds after merging synonyms (Kill = stop and kill,
54	// Delete = delete and remove, Terminal = terminal and shell) and because
55	// display toggles are excluded from the count.
56	const (
57		New      = "N" // Create a resource from this context
58		Edit     = "E" // Edit the selected resource
59		Delete   = "D" // Delete the selected resource
60		Rename   = "M" // Rename (mv)
61		Scan     = "S" // Scan the selected target
62		ScanAll  = "A" // Scan everything (modal: "purge the cache first" checkbox)
63		Fetch    = "F" // Catch up with the source: fetch + fast-forward, or follow a stream
64		Clone    = "C" // Enter clone selection
65		Terminal = "T" // Open a terminal or shell
66		IDE      = "O" // Open in the configured IDE
67		Web      = "W" // Open a URL in the browser
68		Logs     = "L" // Open the logs
69		Pager    = "V" // Open in the system pager
70		Kill     = "K" // Stop, kill (modal: Stop / Restart, or SIGKILL)
71		Prune    = "P" // Remove unused resources
72		Browser  = "B" // Open the multi-registry browser
73		Get      = "G" // Pull (get) the image or tag
74		Auth     = "U" // Login / logout of the registry — toggles based on the row's state
75		Exclude  = "X" // Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore
76		Requests = "R" // Open merge requests · PRs
77		Issues   = "I" // Open issues
78		Diagnose = "H" // Open network diagnostics on this target
79		// Jump took J from the free letters: it opens the selected row's related
80		// resource in the view that owns it — the image a container runs, today.
81		Jump = "J" // Jump to the related resource in its own view

84		// two are never reachable at the same time.

93	// alt+:, which has the opposite flaw: on Terminal.app and iTerm2,
94	// Option+Shift+; emits a literal character and the key doesn't arrive
95	// either. ctrl+p is free throughout the application, is not a tty control

97	// already learned — command palette.

105	// check the code against; the table in §3.26 is its readable form.
106	var actions = map[string]string{
107		New:      "Create a resource from this context",
108		Edit:     "Edit the selected resource",
109		Delete:   "Delete the selected resource",
110		Rename:   "Rename",
111		Scan:     "Scan the selected target",
112		ScanAll:  "Scan everything",
113		Fetch:    "Catch up with the source",
114		Clone:    "Enter clone selection",
115		Terminal: "Open a terminal or shell",
116		IDE:      "Open in the configured IDE",
117		Web:      "Open a URL in the browser",
118		Logs:     "Open the logs",
119		Pager:    "Open in the system pager",
120		Kill:     "Stop or kill",
121		Prune:    "Remove unused resources",
122		Browser:  "Open the multi-registry browser",
123		Get:      "Pull the image or tag",
124		Auth:     "Log in or out of the registry",
125		Exclude:  "Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore",
126		Requests: "Open merge requests · PRs",
127		Issues:   "Open issues",

144	}

190		return out

194	//
195	// Path is what ties a file to its surface, and it is there so the

213	// up to date.

217		{"netdiag/ports", "ui/netdiag/ports_model.go", []string{"t", "u", "l", "e", "n", "z"}},
218		{"netdiag/checks", "ui/netdiag/", []string{"p"}},
219		{"oci/browser", "ui/oci_resources/browser_", []string{"r"}},
220		{"security/findings", "ui/security/", []string{"c", "h", "m", "l", "p"}},
221		// g opens the fuzzy-find prompt across the whole workspaces tree. Same
222		// justification as the viewer's g: the jump takes an argument (the typed
223		// query), which is not a role home/end/G could ever cover.
224		{"workspaces", "ui/workspaces/", []string{"g"}},
225		// The same prompt over the forge index: every namespace and repository
226		// the session can see, at any depth.
227		{"forge/explorer", "ui/forge/explorer/", []string{"g"}},
228	}

230	// LocalToggles returns the declared surfaces.
231	func LocalToggles() []Surface {
232		return append([]Surface(nil), localToggles...)
233	}

235	// SurfaceFor ties a file path to its surface, by longest prefix. The
236	// second return says whether a surface was found.

238		var best Surface
239		found := false
240		for _, s := range localToggles {
241			if !strings.Contains(path, s.Path) {
242				continue
243			}
244			if !found || len(s.Path) > len(best.Path) {
245				best, found = s, true
246			}
247		}
248		return best, found
249	}

253		Key     string
254		Surface string
255		Why     string
256	}

126	No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
127	implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
128	writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
129	the credential manager *and* in plaintext:
130	
131	| Storage | Backend | Notes |
132	|---------|---------|-------|
133	| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
134	| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when no configured helper is `store` (plaintext) or `cache` (memory with a timeout), by name, path or shell command: `approve` reaches every helper. Context-aware. |
135	| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |
136	
137	`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
138	The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
139	context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
140	pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
141	to the other one. Every host store operation (the probe, `Save`, `Load`,
142	`Delete`) is bounded to 3 s: a store that does not answer, such as a locked
143	Secret Service waiting on an unlock prompt over SSH, is skipped like an absent
144	one, `Detail` says so, and it is not asked again while that call is stuck
145	(`internal/credentials/hoststore_bound.go`, DEVDESK-745).
146	
147	The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
148	`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
149	second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
150	first one holds.
151	
152	`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
153	`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
154	is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
155	the auth view. It takes the `Selection` and moves nothing when it does not
156	persist (memory), and removes a secret from the YAML only once it reads back
157	from the store; otherwise it stays and the note says so (DEVDESK-745).
158

160	
161	Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
162	- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
163	- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests
